definitions: A mechanism that hides the complex implementation details of a particular functionality, exposing only a simplified interface to the user or other parts of a system.

In computing, a conceptual boundary that separates different levels of detail or functionality within a system, allowing each level to operate without needing to understand the complexities of the levels below it.
examples: The operating system provides a layer of abstraction over the hardware.
This software module adds another layer of abstraction to the data access.
Understanding each layer of abstraction is crucial for debugging.
